hero.headline: From business problem to working AI product in one week.
hero.subhead: A build sprint for McCombs MBA students, working on real problems from partner companies. A full-day boot camp on Friday, Feb 5 gives every participant the tools to build. Coding experience is not required.
hero.demoCaption: Teams start with a problem statement like this and finish with a working product.

prompts.problem: Cut invoice review from 3 days to 3 hours
Answer tenant maintenance requests in under a minute
Summarize 200 customer calls into a weekly product brief

canIDoThis.heading: Can I do this?
canIDoThis.subhead: The three questions applicants ask most.

options.label: True
options.answer: You do not need to. The boot camp covers the tools from the ground up, and the tools generate the code. Participants describe the problem and the product; the AI tools do the implementation.

options.label: False
options.answer: Experienced builders anchor teams. You will go deeper on the tools and ship faster, and you will be matched with teammates who bring the business context.

questions.question: I do not have a team.

options.label: True
options.answer: Apply individually. We place individual applicants on teams of two to four, balancing experience across each team.

options.label: False
options.answer: Apply together. Each team member submits their own application with the same team name. Teams are preferred in selection.

questions.question: I can attend the full boot camp on Friday, Feb 5.

options.label: Yes
options.answer: That is the one requirement. The boot camp is where participants get their tools, their team and their problem statement.

options.label: Not sure yet
options.answer: Full attendance is required for selection, so confirm your availability before applying. You may answer "Maybe" on the application, but confirmed applicants are prioritized.

result.heading: You meet the requirements.
result.body: The boot camp covers the rest. The application takes about three minutes.

whatIsIt.heading: What participants do
body: Each team receives a real problem from a partner company and has one week to turn it into a working AI product. The deliverable is something people can use, not a slide deck.

The boot camp on Friday, Feb 5 covers the AI tools from the ground up and gives every participant the same starting point. Teams then build on their own schedule, with mentors available through the week, and present on demo day.
No coding or technical background is required. Teams of two to four are preferred; individual applicants are placed on teams.

whoCanApply.heading: Who can apply
whoCanApply.lead: Open to all McCombs MBA students

groups.title: Full-time MBA
groups.body: First-year and second-year full-time MBA students receive priority for seats.

groups.title: All other McCombs MBA programs
groups.body: Evening, Weekend and Executive MBA students are eligible. The boot camp runs all day on Friday, Feb 5, and full attendance is required.

notes: No coding or technical background is required.
Teams of two to four are preferred. Individual applicants are placed on teams.
One application per person, including each member of a team.

journey.heading: How it works
journey.subhead: Four stages, from boot camp to demo day.

steps.title: Boot camp
steps.body: A full day on campus. Learn the AI tools, meet the partner companies and review their problem statements. Every participant leaves with the same toolkit.

steps.title: Team up
steps.body: Teams of two to four are confirmed and individual applicants are placed. Each team selects a partner problem to work on.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: One week to turn the problem into a working product. Mentors and office hours are available through the week. Teams work on their own schedule.

steps.title: Demo day
steps.body: Teams present to the partner companies, McCombs leadership and the Austin technology community. Winners are announced.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: One full day on Friday, Feb 5 for the boot camp, then about a week of building on your team's schedule. Most teams spend 15 to 25 hours during the build week. Demo day is a few hours.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: No. The boot camp teaches the AI tools from scratch, and the tools handle implementation. Participants focus on defining the problem and the product.

items.q: Which AI tools do we use, and who pays?
items.a: TODO Tool access and credits are being confirmed with partners. Participants will not pay out of pocket. Details will be published here before applications close.

items.q: What if I do not have a team?
items.a: Apply individually. Individual applicants are placed on teams of two to four, with experience balanced across each team. Teams are preferred, so if you have teammates in mind, apply together.

items.q: How big can a team be?
items.a: Two to four people. Everyone on the team submits their own application with the same team name.
A laptop and charger. Tools and credits are provided.

form.title: Apply
introBullets: Seats are limited, please apply by {closeDate}.
We will email participants once selections are made.
Answers are saved if you need to come back later.
Please reach out to {email} if you have any questions.

contact.label: Your UT EID and email
contact.help: This email will be used for all communications.

applyingAs.label: Are you applying with a team or on your own?
applyingAs.help: Teams are 2 to 4 people and are preferred in selection.

teamName.label: What's your team name?
teamName.help: Please have each team member apply and provide the same team name so we can match you.

teammateEmails.label: What are your teammates' emails?
teammateEmails.help: 1 to 3 addresses, not including yours (teams are 2 to 4 people).

captain.label: Will you be your team's captain?
help: As captain, you'll be the main point of contact and help guide your team.
We want every team to bring a mix of skills. Ideally the captain is comfortable using AI tools like Claude Code or Codex.
A technical background isn't required. Knowing each team's skill level helps us support every team in the best way.

captainCommit.label: Thanks for stepping up as captain
captainCommit.text: Captains are our main point of contact, help the team show up for the boot camp and final presentation, and keep things moving during the build.
captainCommit.checkboxLabel: I'm in as my team's captain

bootCamp.label: The boot camp runs {bootCamp}, {bootCampTime} on campus. Will you be available to attend the full session?
bootCamp.help: Full attendance is required. Every participant gets their tools and their use case here.

buildWindow.label: The hackathon build runs {buildStart} to {buildEnd}. Will you have time to work on your use case during this period?
buildWindow.help: Teams build on their own schedule, with mentors available along the way.

finalPresentation.label: The final presentation is {finalPresentation}. Will you be available to attend?
finalPresentation.help: Finalist teams present to a panel of alumni judges. Hold the date in case your team is selected.

useCases.label: Which business areas interest you most?
useCases.help: Pick at least 3, in order of interest: tap your first choice first. Use cases aren't confirmed yet. We'll do our best to match your preferences, but we can't guarantee them.

aiSubscription.label: Do you pay for any AI tools today?
aiSubscription.help: Choose the closest match. This helps us plan tool access and support.

buildExperience.label: How much have you built with AI tools?
buildExperience.help: There's no wrong answer. This helps us balance teams.

aiComfort.label: How comfortable are you using AI tools today?
aiComfort.help: We'll ask again after the hackathon to see how it changed.

resume.label: Upload your resume
resume.help: Optional. PDF, up to 5 MB. It helps us understand the skills on each team.
resume.shareLabel: OK to share my resume with program partners
resume.shareHelp: Partner companies may be interested in participants. We only share your resume if you check this box.
resume.note: Your file isn't saved in this browser. If you leave and come back, attach it again.
